single_biggest_error: The lane never once queried Stock.Quantity. It diagnosed every thin category as an assortment or price-point decision, when the ledger says the store's actual failure is replenishment. Store-wide, 15,876 of 19,487 active SKUs carry ZERO stock right now and 3,149 of those sold in the last 12 months. Inside the lane's own trend categories the stock-out rate is 50-100%: makhana 2 of 2 selling SKUs out of stock (all ₹47,090 of it), sunscreen 16 of 24 (₹48,550 of ₹88,712 = 55%), serum 27 of 37, Korean noodles 7 of 10, Amul Sweet Lassi (₹25,575) out. The clearest case is the lane's own headline: the Korean noodle "collapse" in May-June 2026 was not demand — the purchase ledger shows 240 units bought in April, sold out by 30 April, and NOTHING reordered until 17 July, an 84-day stock-out, while store-wide May 2026 was ARY's biggest month ever (₹95.4 L). The lane's answer to that was "double the Korean shelf, add 8-10 more SKUs" to a buyer who cannot keep five in stock and has three of the five at zero on the day of the audit.

The defensible claim is far narrower — ARY carries no protein-POSITIONED branded FMCG SKU (no high-protein lassi, protein biscuits or protein atta; one RiteBite bar). verdicts.claim: GST 2.0 built a 35-point wedge and the tax code now pays ARY to sell lassi, buttermilk and flavoured milk instead of colas (Finding 6 soWhat, REC 7)
verdicts.original_number: Rs 12.68 L/yr at 40% GST vs Rs 1.02 L/yr of RTD dairy at 5%; monthlyImpactInr 10,000 from shifting volume
verdicts.live_number: Slab counts CONFIRMED (63 SKUs, Rs 13,27,571 at 40%; RTD dairy Rs 1.04 L). But margins are the same: SaleDetail.IncludeInRate=true (Coke Rs 20 -> taxable Rs 14.286) while PurchaseDetail.IncludeInRate=false. Ex-GST gross margin: Coca-Cola 250ml 12.5%, Sprite/Limca/Thums Up 12.5%, Red Bull 16.0% vs Amul Lassi 200ml 11.8%, Amul Sweet Lassi 250ml 11.3%, Cream Bell flavoured milk 10.9%, Smoodh 16.2%, Amul Kool 16.7%. Carbonates Apr-Aug 2025 Rs 6,82,710 -> Apr-Aug 2026 Rs 8,99,663 = +31.8% YoY
verdicts.query_used: SELECT d.MRP, d.SaleRate, d.TaxRate, d.TaxAmount, d.IncludeInRate, d.TaxableValue1 FROM SaleDetail d WHERE TaxRate=40; SELECT pd.PurchaseCost, pd.TaxRate, pd.TaxAmount, pd.IncludeInRate FROM PurchaseDetail pd JOIN PurchaseHeader ph; then CROSS APPLY last PurchaseCost vs 12m avg realisation per named SKU
verdicts.why: GST is a pass-through absorbed by the MRP, not by the retailer. Once you divide the GST-inclusive sale rate by (1+rate) and compare to the GST-exclusive purchase cost, a 40% cola earns ARY 12.5% and a 5% lassi earns 11.3-11.8% — the wedge is worth roughly nothing to ARY, and on the two biggest lassi SKUs the swap is margin-NEGATIVE. There is also no volume suppression to harvest: carbonates grew 32% YoY through the 40% slab. My own first pass got this wrong by using (rate-cost)/rate before checking IncludeInRate; the corrected figures are above.

verdicts.claim: Diapers: ARY sells ~30 a month against a single baby's 150-200 a month, from 73 listed SKUs of which 11 sold
verdicts.live_number: 34.6 PACKS/month (415 packs / 12m), Rs 2,684/month — the rupee figure reproduces. But every SKU is a multi-pant pack: Pampers L Size 7 Pants at Rs 99, M Size 8 Pants at Rs 99, S Size 4 Pants at Rs 46, M Size 2 Pants at Rs 25. 415 packs is roughly 2,200 individual pants a year = ~183 pants/month

verdicts.claim: Basket depth has not moved in four years: 2.70 lines/bill 2023 to 2.68 in 2026, while the national rural basket went 5.8 items (2022) to 9.3 (2024). +0.1 lines/bill = Rs 2.35 L/month
verdicts.original_number: 2.70 (2023) -> 2.68 (2026); avg bill Rs 192 -> Rs 222; bills 257k -> 311k; Rs 2.35 L/month impact
verdicts.live_number: 2023: 2.696 lines, Rs 192.01, 257,247 bills. 2024: 2.663, Rs 210.64, 282,299. 2025: 2.641, Rs 222.28, 311,286. 2026 YTD: 2.681, Rs 209.43, 248,564. Avg line Rs 77.46, 30,986 bills/month. The Kantar figure is real — GroupM/Kantar Rural Barometer 2024, 5.8 (2022) to 9.3 (2024), and the cited biizline page does carry it
verdicts.query_used: SELECT YEAR(h.VoucherDate), COUNT(DISTINCT h.SerialNumber), COUNT(*), lines_per_bill, avg_bill FROM SaleHeader h JOIN SaleDetail d ON d.SerialNumber=h.SerialNumber WHERE VoucherDate>='2022-01-01' GROUP BY YEAR; citation checked via WebFetch of biizline.com and WebSearch of the Kantar/GroupM Rural Barometer
verdicts.why: Every ARY number reproduces — this is the lane's cleanest internal work. Three qualifications. (a) The Kantar metric counts FMCG CATEGORIES bought per rural household per year, not lines on a till receipt, so the comparison is apples-to-oranges; the lane half-flags this but mischaracterises the source as 'a rural shopping trip'. (b) The Rs 2.35 L is gross revenue at the average line value with no margin applied and assumes the added line is fully incremental. (c) It double-counts: REC 0 says 'every category below is a candidate for line 3', then RECs 1-11 are sized separately at a further Rs 1.68 L/month, and the twelve figures are presented additively.

verdicts.claim: Every category the lane calls thin is thin because of a buying or price-point decision (structural premise underneath all 12 recommendations)
verdicts.original_number: not stated — the lane never tests availability
verdicts.live_number: 15,876 of 19,487 active SKUs carry ZERO stock right now, and 3,149 of them sold in the last 12 months. Inside the lane's own trend categories, SKUs that sold in 12m but are out of stock today: makhana 2 of 2 (Rs 47,090 of Rs 47,090), sunscreen 16 of 24 (Rs 48,550 of Rs 88,712), serum 27 of 37 (Rs 25,326), Korean noodles 7 of 10 (Rs 18,386), diapers 5 of 11, Amul Sweet Lassi (Rs 25,575), one of three RTD ORS
verdicts.query_used: SELECT CASE WHEN onhand>0 THEN 'has stock' WHEN =0 THEN 'ZERO stock' ELSE 'negative' END, COUNT(*), COUNT(CASE WHEN sales>0 THEN 1 END) FROM ProductMaster p OUTER APPLY (SELECT SUM(k.Quantity) FROM Stock k WHERE k.ProductID=p.ProductID) OUTER APPLY (12m sales) WHERE p.IsActive=1 GROUP BY 1; plus a per-category version over 8 trend patterns
verdicts.why: Stock.Quantity is the one field the schema notes flag as the real on-hand, and the lane never reads it once across 18 findings, 5 tables and 12 recommendations. Half or more of what ARY already sells in these categories is unavailable today. That inverts the top recommendation: before adding 8-10 Korean SKUs, a Rs 99-199 sunscreen rung and a K-beauty test shelf, the store has to be able to keep the ones it has on the shelf — the Korean line alone went 84 days without a reorder after selling out in three weeks.
